title: Choose the visual world for your portfolio
question: The roll assigned a transit-wayfinding world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Line: a wayfinding system
options.lineage: Luas / Dublin Bus route maps and enamel station signage
options.thesis: Your work as a route network: projects are stations, categories are lines, your career is the journey.
options.viewport: The network map leads: four coloured lines (Enterprise, Mobile, Web, IoT) carry all 7 projects as stations; VISE sits at the interchange marked Now; selecting any station opens its platform sign with image, role, timeline and link. Name, UX Engineer and résumé sit in the station-name bar above.
options.risk: Becomes a costume if the map is decorative; every station must be a real, readable link.

raised.raise: Motion snaps a whole step and settles, never glides; the featured station is ranked by inversion (dark panel), not by colour.
Every project gets a fixed station code (M1, W2…) in a fixed position, so numbering is the index.
One continuous line runs the whole page, from network to journey to terminus.
Every station carries its provenance label: role, year, and where it opens.
Hierarchy is carried by scale, never by colour alone.
Amid the dense map, one calm panel is the only luxury: the open station sign.

options.label: Swiss Grid Poster
options.thesis: A strict modular grid where each project is set like a concert poster: big numerals, one red, absolute order.
options.viewport: A 12-column poster: huge project numerals and titles stepped across the grid, VISE as the largest block, name and role set small in the top margin.
options.risk: The most familiar 'designer portfolio' language; strong but where many portfolios land.

options.label: Depot Destination Blind
options.thesis: Projects roll past one fixed window like a bus blind.
options.viewport: One project visible at a time in a fixed window.
options.case: Fuses poorly: shows one project at a time, which hides the work from a skimming recruiter.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.viewport: Banks of counters for projects and years.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the portfolio has few real metrics, and inventing numbers breaks product truth.
options.kept: Fixed index positions: numbering as navigation.

options.label: Hand-bent Neon Circuit
options.thesis: Your name as one continuous glass stroke.
options.viewport: A dark room with one glowing script.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dramatic, but the work disappears behind the sign.
options.kept: One continuous stroke through the whole page.

options.label: Memory Quilt Atlas
options.thesis: Each project a stitched block with its history.
options.viewport: A quilt of unequal project blocks.
options.case: Fuses partly: human and warm, but reads craft-hobby rather than senior UX Engineer.
options.kept: Every item seamed to its provenance label.

options.label: Massin Stage Page
options.thesis: Designer and engineer as two typeset voices.
options.viewport: Two voices arguing across the spread.
options.case: Fuses poorly: clever, but makes facts hard to find.
options.kept: Scale carries emphasis, never colour alone.

options.label: Fly-posted Festival Hoarding
options.thesis: A loud collage with one calm panel.
options.viewport: Full-bleed collage with a floating white card.
options.case: Fuses poorly: energetic but reads playful, not senior.
options.kept: One calm panel as the only luxury amid density.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern portfolio: intro, project grid, experience, contact, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Short intro, then a tidy grid of project cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from most portfolios by design.
